answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so a node’s influence depends on paths from independently trusted roots rather than self-asserted identities. A Sybil cluster connected by only a few external edges has low conductance; spectral mixing and min-cut bounds therefore limit the probability that walk mass enters it, and hence cap its aggregate voting weight. Labels such as umber, ferrous, and cipher do not alter this structural bound.
